You're on the right track! You've correctly captured the main idea: an object in motion tends to stay in motion.

Your statement "Force makes things keep moving" is a really common misconception. Newton's insight was that you don't need a force to *keep* something moving. An object will happily coast forever at a constant velocity.

A force is only needed to *change* an object's motion — to make it speed up, slow down, or change direction.

Consider this: if you push a book across a table, it quickly stops. If you slide a hockey puck across the ice, it goes much farther. Why the difference?
